extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates / graduate students and researchers in algebraic topology and homotopy theory
extracted.subtask_description: Deriving and applying the Leray–Hirsch theorem, Thom isomorphism, orientability, and the Gysin sequence for (disk/sphere) fiber bundles; plus Brown representability and spectra-representability of cohomology theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative Leray–Hirsch criterion (Theorem 4D.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (F, F')→(E, E')→B is a fiber-bundle pair with H*(F, F'; R) a free R-module, finitely generated in each degree, and there exist classes c_j ∈ H*(E, E'; R) whose restrictions form a basis for H*(F, F'; R) in each fiber, then H*(E, E'; R) is a free H*(B; R)-module with basis {c_j}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module structure is via p*(b) ∪ c (relative cup product H*(E;R)×H*(E,E';R)→H*(E,E';R)). This is the relative version of the absolute Leray–Hirsch theorem; the hypotheses include finite generation and that the fiberwise restrictions of the chosen classes give a basis in each fiber. Use excision and mapping-cylinder arguments when comparing with absolute situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thom class definition for a disk bundle
rubrics_metrics.description: An element c ∈ H^n(E, E'; R) whose restriction to each fiber (D^n, S^{n-1}) is a generator of H^n(D^n, S^{n-1}; R) ≈ R is called a Thom class for the bundle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For R = Z a 'generator' means an element mapping to ±1 under the canonical isomorphism; for a general commutative ring R, a 'generator' means a unit multiple (invertible). A Thom class with Z coefficients induces Thom classes with other coefficient rings via the map H^n(E,E';Z)→H^n(E,E';R).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thom isomorphism (Corollary 4D.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a disk bundle p:E→B (with pair (E,E')) has a Thom class c ∈ H^n(E,E';R), then the map Φ: H^i(B;R)→H^{i+n}(E,E';R) given by Φ(b)=p*(b) ∪ c is an isomorphism for all i≥0, and H^i(E,E';R)=0 for i<n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the main algebraic consequence of having a Thom class. The Thom isomorphism can be recast in terms of the Thom space T(E)=E/E' as H^i(B;R) ≅ H^{i+n}(T(E);R). Use this to translate relative cohomology classes into absolute cohomology of the Thom space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientability of a sphere bundle (criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sphere bundle S^{n-1}→E'→B is orientable if for every loop γ in B the induced homotopy equivalence L_γ on the fiber S^{n-1} induces the identity map on H_{n-1}(S^{n-1}; Z) (equivalently on H^{n-1}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent characterizations: product bundles are orientable; sphere bundles over simply-connected bases are orientable. Example: Klein bottle seen as S^1-bundle over S^1 is nonorientable because the monodromy reverses orientation; torus is orientable. Orientability of a disk bundle is defined via orientability of its boundary sphere subbundle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of Thom class vs orientability (Theorem 4D.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every disk bundle has a Thom class with Z_2 coefficients; orientable disk bundles have Thom classes with Z coefficients. Conversely (exercise), the existence of a Thom class with Z-coefficients implies orientability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus Z_2-coefficients remove orientability obstruction. For Z-coefficients one needs orientability of the disk bundle (equivalently of its boundary sphere bundle). The proof uses pullbacks to CW approximations and the five-lemma plus the lifting/monodromy description of orientability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiberwise restriction isomorphism (property (∗))
rubrics_metrics.description: If D^n→E→B is an orientable disk bundle over a connected CW complex B, then the restriction map H^i(E,E';Z)→H^i(D^n_x,S^{n-1}_x;Z) is an isomorphism for every fiber and all i ≤ n. For Z_2 coefficients the same statement holds without orientability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This property yields a canonical preferred isomorphism H^n(E,E';Z) ≅ Z (after choosing an isomorphism on one fiber and transporting by monodromy) and ensures that a generator of H^n(E,E') is a Thom class. The proof proceeds by induction on the dimension of the base using Mayer–Vietoris and excision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gysin sequence and Euler class definition
rubrics_metrics.description: For a sphere bundle S^{n-1}→E→B (with mapping cylinder Mp a disk bundle and a Thom class c ∈ H^n(Mp,E;R)), the long exact sequence for (Mp,E) together with the Thom isomorphism yields the Gysin sequence. The Euler class e ∈ H^n(B;R) is defined by e = (p*)^{-1} j*(c), where j*:H^n(Mp,E)→H^n(Mp) is inclusion; equivalently, under the Thom isomorphism e corresponds to c ∪ c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the Gysin sequence the map 'cup with e' appears (· ∪ e : H^*(B)→H^{*+n}(B)). The square relating p* and cup-with-e commutes: p*(b) ∪ j*(c) = p*(b ∪ e). These identities tie the Thom class and Euler class algebraically and determine how cohomology of total and base interact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of the Gysin sequence (generalized criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Gysin sequence applies to any orientable fiber bundle F→E→B whose fiber F is a CW complex with H*(F;R) ≈ H*(S^{n-1};R). Orientability is defined via monodromy maps L_γ acting trivially on H_{n-1}(F;R).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To derive the Gysin sequence in this generalized setting, replace the associated disk bundle by the mapping cylinder CF→Mp→B. The same derivation using Thom isomorphism and long exact sequence of the pair holds without extra modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology algebra transfer via Gysin (Proposition 4D.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If S^{2k-1}→E→B is an orientable sphere bundle and H*(E;R) is a polynomial ring R[x_1,...,x_ℓ] on even-dimensional generators, then H*(B;R)=R[y_1,...,y_ℓ,e] where e is the Euler class and p*(y_i)=x_i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key steps: odd-degree vanishing in H*(B) follows from surjectivity of ∪e, yielding short exact sequences 0→H^{2i}(B) --∪e--> H^{2i+2k}(B) --p*--> H^{2i+2k}(E)→0. Algebraic induction and exactness show that all classes in H*(B) are polynomials in lifts y_i and e, and injectivity follows from divisibility by e and induction on degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of coefficient rings where 2 is invertible
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain cohomology calculations (e.g., for Gn(R^∞) with odd prime p or Q coefficients) require working over coefficient rings where 2 has a multiplicative inverse so that H*(V_2(R^{2k+1});R) ≈ H*(S^{4k-1};R).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When 2 is invertible torsion phenomena of order 2 disappear and calculations simplify to polynomial algebras on even-degree generators (pi and e). Integral cohomology may have 2-torsion; integral statements often require extra analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology theory axioms (reformulated)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reduced cohomology theory on basepointed CW complexes is a sequence of functors h^n with natural suspension isomorphisms h^n(X) ≅ h^{n+1}(ΣX) satisfying: (i) homotopy invariance, (ii) exactness: for inclusion A↪X the sequence h^n(X/A)→h^n(X)→h^n(A) is exact, (iii) wedge axiom: h^n(∨_α X_α) ≅ ∏_α h^n(X_α).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These axioms suffice to reconstruct the usual long exact sequences for pairs via cofibration sequences. The Mayer–Vietoris property (gluing existence) follows from these axioms and is used in representability proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brown representability conditions (Theorem 4E.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a contravariant functor h from connected basepointed CW complexes to pointed sets satisfies the homotopy axiom, the Mayer–Vietoris axiom, and the wedge axiom, then there exists a connected CW complex K and u∈h(K) such that the natural map T_u: [X,K]→h(X), T_u(f)=f^*(u), is a bijection for all X (i.e., (K,u) is universal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universality implies K is unique up to homotopy. Proof strategy: construct π_*–universal approximations by attaching cells to kill kernels of π_i-maps, then apply Mayer–Vietoris and wedge axioms plus mapping telescope arguments to assemble K and element u. The result underlies representability of cohomology theories by spaces/spectra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of π_*–universal pair (Lemma 4E.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given (Z,z) with Z a connected CW complex and z∈h(Z), one can inductively attach cells to Z to produce a CW complex K containing Z and u∈h(K) extending z such that (K,u) is π_*–universal (i.e., T_u: π_i(K)→h(S^i) is iso for i<n and surjective for i=n for all n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: at step n, attach (n+1)-cells along maps representing elements of ker(T_{u_n}:π_n(K_n)→h(S^n)) and then extend the class using the wedge axiom to obtain u_{n+1}. Use mapping telescope to pass to the union K. This inductive cell-killing is the core of Brown's representability construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension property for π_*–universal pairs (Lemma 4E.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (K,u) is π_*–universal and (X,A) a basepointed CW pair, then for any x∈h(X) and any map f:A→K with f^*(u)=x|_A there exists an extension g:X→K with g^*(u)=x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lemma is the Mayer–Vietoris/gluing step in proving universality: form Z = X ∪_A K, get z∈h(Z) restricting to x and u, embed (Z,z) in a π_*–universal K' and retract K' to K (since both are π_*–universal), producing the required extension by homotopy. This yields surjectivity and injectivity of T_u.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representability of cohomology theories by spectra (Theorem 4E.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every reduced cohomology theory on basepointed CW complexes is representable: h^n(X) ≅ [X, K_n] for a spectrum {K_n} (the spaces K_n are unique up to homotopy). The structure maps ε_n: K_n→ΩK_{n+1} are weak equivalences arising from natural suspension isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One constructs each K_n as the representing space for h^n and uses naturality of suspension isomorphisms to identify K_n ≃ ΩK_{n+1} up to weak equivalence, thus assembling the spectrum. The group structure on cohomology corresponds to loop-space/group structure on mapping sets for suspensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stable homotopy groups define a reduced homology theory (Proposition 4F.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The stable homotopy groups π^s_n(X) define a reduced homology theory on basepointed CW complexes: suspension isomorphisms hold, exactness (long exact sequences of pairs) holds after enough suspensions, and the wedge axiom holds (finite-reduction + compactness argument).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More generally, for a fixed complex K, h_n(X)=π^s_n(X∧K) is a reduced homology theory with coefficients h_n(S^0)=π^s_n(K). For suitable choices (e.g., K=K(G,n)), this homology theory agrees with ordinary homology in low degrees where connectivity hypotheses ensure stable/unstable groups coincide.
